seoGeo.title: SEO & GEO Setup for Your Website — Stanislav Sinitsyn
seoGeo.description: Technical SEO and GEO setup: indexable pages, structured data, multilingual markup and clear content that search engines and AI assistants can read. No ranking promises.
seoGeo.h1: SEO and GEO setup for your website
seoGeo.intro: I set up websites so that search engines and AI assistants can find, read and understand them: the technical foundation, structured data and clear content. Because I build sites too, the search side is set up together with the code.
seoGeo.b1p: Pages that search engines can crawl and index: correct status codes, canonical URLs, robots rules, a sitemap and a clean page structure.
seoGeo.b2p: Language versions with hreflang, localized metadata and a clear default, so each audience gets the right version of a page.
seoGeo.b3p: Schema.org markup for the person or company, services, pages and breadcrumbs, validated before release.
seoGeo.b4: Content for search and AI answers
seoGeo.b4p: Clear service pages and direct answers to real questions, structured so people and AI assistants can quote them accurately.
seoGeo.b5p: Search Console, Bing and Yandex Webmaster connected, with a baseline for search visibility and AI answers to compare against later.
seoGeo.p1p: We review what search engines and AI assistants currently see on your site: crawl access, markup, content and language versions.
seoGeo.p2p: Fixes are prioritised by impact and dependencies, so the foundation comes before the finishing touches.
seoGeo.p3p: I make the changes in the code and the content, and check each one on the rendered site.
seoGeo.p4p: Measurement is connected, a baseline is recorded and results are reviewed after search engines have re-crawled the site.
seoGeo.a1: GEO, generative engine optimization, means preparing a site so that AI assistants and AI search can find, understand and cite it. It builds on SEO rather than replacing it, and its methods and measurement are still evolving.
seoGeo.q2: Can you guarantee rankings or AI mentions?
seoGeo.a2: No. Nobody controls search engines or AI models. I fix what is within the site’s control and measure the results, but positions and citations cannot be guaranteed.
seoGeo.q3: Do you work on existing sites or only new ones?
seoGeo.a3: Both. For an existing site we start with an audit of what search engines see today. For a new site I build the search foundation in from the start.
seoGeo.q4: Which search engines do you set up for?
seoGeo.a4: Google and Bing, and Yandex for audiences in Russia and neighbouring countries. Language and country versions are set up separately.

mobile.title: Mobile App Development with React Native & Expo — Stanislav Sinitsyn
mobile.description: iOS and Android apps with React Native and Expo from a single codebase. Design, development and release by an independent developer, working directly with you.
mobile.h1: Mobile apps on React Native and Expo
mobile.intro: I design and build iOS and Android apps from a single codebase: the interface, the API behind it and the integrations between them. You work directly with me.
mobile.b1p: Cross-platform apps on React Native from one codebase, so both platforms get the same features at the same time.
mobile.b2p: Mobile versions of customer portals and personal accounts: sign-in, profiles, orders, bookings and tracking.
mobile.b3p: Internal tools for people on the move: forms, checklists, task lists and reports.
mobile.b4p: Push notifications, camera, location, file access and offline use, wired in where the product needs them.
mobile.b5p: The API behind the app and third-party services: authentication, analytics and the systems your business already uses.
mobile.p1p: We start with what the app must achieve, who uses it, and what already exists, such as a website or an API.
mobile.p2p: Screens, user flows, data and integrations are agreed before development starts.
mobile.p3p: I build in stages you can install and try on your own phone, so decisions are made on a working app.
mobile.p4p: Testing, publishing to the App Store and Google Play, analytics and a clear handover. Further releases as needed.
mobile.a1: One codebase serves iOS and Android, and Expo simplifies builds, updates and release. If a product needs deep native features, we discuss that before starting.
mobile.q2: Can you work from my design?
mobile.a2: Yes. If you have designs, I build from them. If not, we start from the idea and work through screens, user flows and interface together.
mobile.q3: Can you extend an existing app or website?
mobile.a3: Yes. I can add features to an existing app, or build a mobile app on top of your current website or API. We start from what you have now.
mobile.q4: Will the app be published in the stores?
mobile.a4: Yes, publishing to the App Store and Google Play is part of the launch. Store review is controlled by Apple and Google, so approval and timing cannot be guaranteed.

webDev.title: Web Development with React & Next.js — Stanislav Sinitsyn
webDev.description: Websites, web apps, SaaS and customer portals on React, Next.js, Vue and Node.js. Full-stack development by an independent developer, from first sketch to launch.
webDev.intro: I design and build websites, web apps, SaaS products and customer portals: the interface, the API behind it and the integrations between them. You work directly with me.
webDev.b1p: Company and product sites, landing pages and content sites. Clear structure, server-rendered pages and structured data, so search engines and AI assistants can read them.
webDev.b2p: Interactive products in the browser: dashboards, booking flows, reporting and map-based screens.
webDev.b3p: Multi-role systems with customers, orders, documents and reports, from database models and APIs to the interface.
webDev.b4p: Portals where customers book, track and download, including single sign-in across several applications.
webDev.b5p: Third-party services, e-signature, webhooks, build tooling and framework migrations in products that keep shipping.
webDev.p1p: We start with what the site or app must achieve, who uses it, and what already exists.
webDev.p2p: Pages, user flows, data and integrations are agreed before development starts.
webDev.p3p: I build in stages you can open and comment on, so decisions are made on real screens.
webDev.p4p: Testing, deployment, analytics and a clear handover. Further releases as needed.
webDev.a1: React and Next.js, or Vue and Nuxt, with TypeScript and Node.js on the server. The choice depends on the product and on who will maintain it.
webDev.q2: Can you work from my design?
webDev.a2: Yes. If you have designs, I build from them. If not, we start from the idea and work through structure, user flows and interface together.
webDev.q3: Can you improve an existing site?
webDev.a3: Yes: new features, integrations, performance work and migrations. We start from what you have now.
webDev.q4: Will the site be found in search?
webDev.a4: I build pages that can be indexed: clean markup, metadata, structured data and a sitemap. Rankings depend on many factors and cannot be guaranteed.
